title: Unexpected dedicated quota squeeze due to warmup credit leak
creator: Amina Patel
description: Several Dedicated customers reported 429/quota-exhausted errors during a morning traffic spike despite cluster-level headroom. Triage showed per-tenant reserved pools reported much lower available burst credits than expected. Initial mitigation included manual reconciliation of tenant warmup credits and temporary quota increases for affected customers. Root cause investigation indicates a warmup-credit lifecycle leak: when warmup allocations failed to complete (due to sticky KV-cache reservations and a preemption path), the allocator did not release the 'warmup' credit ledger entries. Over several hours this leaked credits, causing the autoscaler and headroom accounting to under-estimate available capacity and underprovision reserved pools, producing customer-facing throttling. This ticket tracks the bugfix, rollout, customer comms, and postmortem action items.
repro_steps: Create a dedicated tenant with small reserved pool and enable kv-cache sticky allocation.
Trigger repeated warmup flows and force a preemption/fallback by artificially lowering capacity on the node (simulate transient GPU OOM).
Observe that warmup credit ledger is incremented but not decremented on failed allocation paths.
Run headroom accounting report and note the delta between ledger sum and actual free slots; autoscaler decisions reflect the stale ledger.
Confirm 429s when burst requests exceed the (incorrectly low) available credit computed by allocator.
investigation_notes: 2025-02-10 08:17 - Alert: multiple 429 spikes across 3 customers in us-west-2. On-call routed to dedicated-capacity team.
2025-02-10 09:03 - Initial triage: cluster capacity high, but reserved-pool headroom low for affected tenants. Metrics: warmup_credit_total != warmup_credit_released for several tenants.

2025-02-10 10:20 - Hypothesis: warmup credit is not being released on allocation failure inside kv-cache sticky path. Reproduced locally by injecting allocation-failure exception during warmup handshake.
2025-02-11 14:44 - Implemented quick recon script to reconcile ledger values; applied to 4 affected tenants — immediate reduction in 429s.

2025-02-12 11:30 - Deeper code review: allocation flow has multiple early-returns on error that skip credit release, and fallback path also expects a different cleanup hook which isn't invoked for sticky KV cache reservations.

2025-02-13 16:12 - Load test with the failing code reproduced leak over ~1 hour; leak rate ~0.3 credits/min for warmup allocations under churn. Extrapolated to 8 hours leads to full exhaustion for small-tenants.

2025-02-14 09:02 - Design meeting: trade-offs discussed — always-release credits on any allocation exit vs. add reference counting around credit ownership. Chosen: explicit ensure-release in all exit paths and add defensive RC check to prevent double-release.
2025-02-15 18:00 - Added unit tests for allocation failure path and integration test simulating preemption; these validate credit lifecycle.
2025-02-17 09:26 - PR created and requested review. PR includes instrumentation: credit+allocation spans emitted to tracing with tenant id and allocation id.
2025-02-17 14:10 - Performance review: additional ensure-release on hot path adds a small conditional (lock-free) check; microbenchmarks show <1.2% p99 token-latency impact under high QPS. Accepted.
2025-02-18 07:45 - Staging rollout smoke passed for 6 hours under synthetic churn; no regressions in headroom metrics. Preparing canary rollout into us-west-2 with 10% traffic.
decision: Patch allocation code to guarantee warmup-credit release on every exit path, add a defensive refcount guard to avoid double-release, and introduce reconciliation job to heal historical ledger drift. Also add tracing and new alerts for ledger drift >5% for any tenant over 30 minutes.
implementation: Reconciler script (one-off): https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/commit/7a8d3f9 - used for emergency reconciles
qa_plan: Unit tests for every allocation exit path ensuring credit release.
Integration test that simulates node preemption + kv-cache sticky allocation and validates ledger parity after failure.
Canary rollout: 10% traffic in us-west-2 for 24 hours with automated rollback on ledger-drift > 2% or customer-429 increase > 1.5x baseline.
Post-canary soak: 72 hours monitoring across regions before full rollout.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge PR to main with green CI and approvals from runtime and allocator owners.
Step 2: Deploy to staging, run smoke suite (30m), validate ledger parity and no perf regression.
Step 3: Canary in us-west-2 (10% traffic) for 24h. Automated rollback on defined SLO regressions.
Step 4: Expand to 50% for 24h, then global rollout if stable.
Step 5: Run reconciler batch for tenants with ledger drift >1% after rollout window and notify affected customers.
